title: Pneumatic Compression Devices

criteria.text: Covered only for lymphedema or CVI with venous stasis ulcers
criteria.span: Pneumatic devices are covered for the treatment of lymphedema or for the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency with venous stasis ulcers.

criteria.text: Lymphedema: four-week conservative trial with no significant improvement or significant remaining symptoms
criteria.span: Pneumatic compression devices are covered in the home setting for the treatment of lymphedema if the patient has undergone a four-week trial of conservative therapy and the treating physician determines that there has been no significant improvement or if significant symptoms remain after the trial.

criteria.text: Lymphedema trial includes compression bandage/garment, exercise, and limb elevation
criteria.span: The trial of conservative therapy must include use of an appropriate compression bandage system or compression garment, exercise, and elevation of the limb.

criteria.text: CVI: venous stasis ulcer(s) failed to heal after a 6-month physician-directed conservative trial
criteria.span: only if the patient has one or more venous stasis ulcer(s) which have failed to heal after a 6 month trial of conservative therapy directed by the treating physician.

criteria.text: Physician prescription and oversight (evaluation, instruction, treatment plan, monitoring)
criteria.span: Pneumatic compression devices are covered only when prescribed by a physician and when they are used with appropriate physician oversight

criteria.text: Physician determination includes objective findings with measurements of severity
criteria.span: Symptoms and objective findings, including measurements which establish the severity of the condition;

criteria.text: Physician determination includes clinical response to an initial treatment with the device
criteria.span: The clinical response to an initial treatment with the device.

criteria.text: Segmented calibrated gradient device (E0652) only with unique characteristics preventing satisfactory treatment with simpler devices
criteria.span: The only time that a segmented, calibrated gradient pneumatic compression device (HCPCs code E0652) would be covered is when the individual has unique characteristics that prevent them from receiving satisfactory pneumatic compression treatment using a nonsegmented device in conjunction with a segmented appliance or a segmented compression device without manual control of pressure in each chamber.

notes: Lymphedema requires a 4-week conservative trial (compression, exercise, elevation); CVI requires venous stasis ulcer(s) unhealed after a 6-month trial (compression, wound dressings, exercise, elevation). General criteria: physician prescription and oversight, plus a physician determination documenting diagnosis/prognosis, objective measurements, failed treatments, and clinical response to an initial treatment with the device. E0652 needs unique characteristics preventing satisfactory treatment with the simpler devices.
